payload.name: Health injury synonym and family-member retrieval
payload.description: When a question asks who was injured, hurt, or affected by a health condition—especially within a family—use synonym expansions for the health event and separate searches for each family member before answering.
content: If a question asks about injuries, accidents, or health problems affecting a person or their family, do not answer from a single search using only the literal wording (e.g., 'injured'); memories may describe the event with related terms such as accident, injury, hurt, surgery, hospital, or specific body parts.

Run at least one supplementary search combining the person's name with synonyms of the health condition (e.g., 'accident', 'injury', 'hurt', 'hospital', 'surgery', 'recovery'), and include queries for each named family member or relation (son, daughter, partner, spouse, child) when the question asks 'who' in a group.

Before answering, check that the retrieved evidence covers every person the question asks about; if only the main subject is found, continue searching with family-relation terms until relevant memories for all individuals are retrieved or exhausted.

solves: This addresses retrieval failures when a health/injury question about a person and their relatives is answered from the first search that matches only the main subject's own injury. Memories about relatives often use different vocabulary (accident, injury, hurt) or are stored under a family-relation term, so the rule requires synonym-expanded and per-relative searches before answering. It applies to any future question asking who in a family or group was injured, hurt, or had a health issue; it is not for general activity, preference, or theme questions that have no injury/health component.
